ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable plan-decomposition assurance under H1-H8 is: for a plan that is a DETERMINISTIC DERIVATION FROM FROZEN INPUTS (a pure function of the committed closure — pre-commitment of the plan artifact is one sufficient realization, not a necessity) into a finite, explicitly typed dataflow DAG with a declared goal-artifact set, ALL defects in the decidable defect class — cyclic dependency, produces/consumes artifact-type mismatch on any edge, goal artifact unreachable from admitted inputs, orphan stage feeding no goal, ambiguous execution order — are made structurally inadmissible at plan-derivation time (fail-closed, H3); the admitted plan has a unique deterministic total schedule (H5); the plan carries a certificate any third party re-derives from the committed inputs alone (H8); AND the decidable class extends to declared-finite-domain planning: VAL-class precondition/effect validation of a candidate plan against a committed finite-domain action model, and sound+complete plan SYNTHESIS over committed finite domains emitting existence certificates (a valid plan with its validation trace) or nonexistence certificates (an exhaustive refutation over the finite state space). No feasible system can additionally verify completeness of the plan relative to informal human intent, nor decide plan existence over unbounded action spaces.
derivation: (1) Verification theory: completeness relative to intent is not computable — the intent is not encoded; only completeness relative to a committed formal goal specification is machine-checkable (same underdetermination as AX-01). (2) Complexity, corrected: general plan synthesis is PSPACE-complete over finite STRIPS domains and undecidable over infinite domains — but PSPACE-completeness is a cost fact, not an impossibility: over a COMMITTED FINITE domain, plan validation is linear-time decidable and plan existence/synthesis is decidable with checkable certificates, so the feasible decidable class strictly exceeds the five structural DAG checks; the ceiling includes finite-domain synthesis-with-certificates, with cost governed by AX-17 budgets. H5 requires the plan be a PURE FUNCTION of frozen inputs — 'committed before execution' is a sufficient discipline, not the requirement itself: a deterministic planner over a committed finite domain yields replayable synthesized plans that satisfy H5/H6 identically. Against a committed finite DAG, every structural property in the defect class is decidable in O(V+E) with linear-time-checkable certificates; therefore FULL exclusion of the decidable class, not statistical reduction, is feasible — elimination of the error class is the ceiling, guarding against instances is below it. (3) Determinism: among valid schedules, uniqueness is achievable at zero cost (topological sort with total lexicographic tie-break); any nondeterministic schedule strictly violates H5. Exceeding this ceiling requires deciding intent (not encoded) or verifying unbounded plan spaces (undecidable).
relativity_note: Relative to a committed typed-DAG plan semantics (finite stages with declared produces/consumes artifact types and a declared goal-artifact set) extended by a committed finite-domain action model for validation/synthesis. 'Plan completeness' is completeness w.r.t. the committed goal set and domain — never w.r.t. unformalized intent. Witness instantiation: appendix.
lean_obligation: Model a plan as P = (S : Finset Stage, produces, consumes, goals, inputs) with edge relation E s t := (produces s intersect consumes t).Nonempty. Prove: (T1) gate soundness+completeness — the admission predicate wf P holds iff acyclicity, exact type-matching on every edge, goal reachability from inputs, and no orphan stage; (T2) schedule uniqueness — for wf P the tie-broken topological sort is the UNIQUE linearization satisfying the spec; (T3) certificate faithfulness — cert(P) verifies iff wf P; (T4) goal completeness — wf P implies every goal artifact has a finite derivation path from admitted inputs; (T5) planner determinism and certificates — for a committed finite-domain model D, the synthesis function synth : D -> Option Plan is a pure total function; synth D = some p implies valid D p (existence certificate checks), and synth D = none implies an exhaustive-refutation certificate over the finite reachable state space (nonexistence checkable). All over Finset/List with decidable predicates — Lean 4 formalizable.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: B0 witness seats: DEFPIPELINE DSL with :produces metadata (systems/orchestrator-spec/pipeline-dsl.lisp), deterministic topological sort (systems/orchestrator-core/dependency-graph.lisp), staged DAG instance (systems/orchestrator-gr-syntagma/pipeline.lisp), 5-stage cognition decomposition (source/cognition.lisp), single public write seat (unified-frbr-generator.lisp). Mechanism: move the produces/consumes match INTO DEFPIPELINE macroexpansion as a fail-closed compile-time error; lexicographic tie-break in dependency-graph.lisp; emit a plan certificate (S-expression of nodes, typed edges, goal set, schedule + SHA-256 via source/hash-authority.lisp) recomputed by an independent checker. Finite-domain synthesis rung: a committed STRIPS-style action model as data plus a deterministic solver with validation traces — new code, admissible under AX-17 budgets.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the stage produces-to-consumer artifact-type match is computed but NOT gated (a type-mismatched plan is currently admissible); no machine-proof of one-entry composition; no plan certificate artifact; parallel-executor.lisp swallows per-stage errors to nil, marks failed stages executed, and runs intra-tier in nondeterministic order — all violating the fail-closed unique-schedule ceiling; the finite-domain synthesis rung is entirely absent from B0.
